evidence.source: 王寧, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The article, published in 2010, reports several oracle-bone shapes for 白 and says the graph appears in divination inscriptions for white, 伯, and a place name. It surveys proposals including a shortened 帛, thumb, flame/light, face or head, and vessel. The author rejects thumb and face/head arguments as insufficiently evidenced and proposes a cooking or measuring vessel 鬴/釜, with the middle stroke marking the seam between vessel and lid. This is the author's hypothesis, not a consensus.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.source: 王寧, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The author notes that archaeological vessel identifications rely on shape when inscriptions are absent; they cannot establish what Shang people called the vessel. Thus the vessel hypothesis does not independently recover the depicted object's ancient name or pronunciation.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.source: 王寧, 復旦大學出土文獻與古文字研究中心
evidence.text: The article reports oracle-bone uses for the color word 白, title/kinship word 伯, and a place name, but gives no individually dated inscription contexts on the inspected page. The author treats color 白 and 伯 as homophonic loans unrelated to the proposed vessel meaning. Earliest dated examples and the sound of the vessel name are not established there.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 小學堂每日一字
evidence.text: This educational database identifies 白 as a thumb pictograph and proposes that the thumb's position as the leading digit motivates 伯 (eldest/leader). It says 白 was often written for 伯 in oracle-bone texts and was later borrowed for the color word, with 人 added to 伯 to distinguish it. This differs from Wang Ning's analysis and remains a source-specific interpretation.
evidence.title: 每日一字

evidence.text: The entry records Mandarin Standard Chinese bái and a restricted literary bó, and Cantonese Guangzhou/Hong Kong Jyutping baak6. It gives Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *bˤrak and Zhengzhang *braːɡ for 白. It summarizes competing word-history proposals: STEDT's Proto-Sino-Tibetan *bawk and Schuessler's alternative *bar with a -k extension, with the latter motivated by difficulty matching the former's lack of medial r to Middle Chinese. These are lexical etymologies, not component analyses of the graph.
evidence.title: 白 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart
evidence.text: The authors' 2014 table identifies its Mandarin column as Pinyin and its Old Chinese column as Baxter–Sagart reconstruction; it gives 白 bái, Middle Chinese baek, and Old Chinese *bˤrak. The table states that its Middle Chinese transcription represents readings in historical sources such as Guangyun rather than a reconstruction. No sound component is proposed for 白 itself.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

gaps: The Fudan article's reported oracle-bone uses are not accompanied by individually dated inscription contexts on the inspected page; earliest attestation dates and sense order for white, 伯, and the place name remain unresolved.
The original referent is unsettled: the thumb account is presented by Academia Sinica, while the 2010 Fudan author rejects it and proposes a vessel. Neither account is demonstrated as consensus.
No independent evidence establishes the ancient name or pronunciation of the proposed vessel. A reconstructed pronunciation of the word 白 cannot establish the name of a depicted object.

The Fudan author proposes a sound/borrowing relation between 白 and 伯 but does not supply a dated phonological argument on the inspected page. The Academia Sinica account offers a semantic thumb-to-eldest explanation instead; the link remains disputed.

The relationship of 百 to 白 is contested in the inspected Fudan article, which proposes a vessel-content interpretation for 百. This research did not establish an earliest dated 百 attestation or a secure semantic development from white.
The Shuowen wording in the dossier remains a Han-era historical explanation; no Shuowen source page was inspected in this invocation to verify its text or compare it directly with excavated forms.

The proposed glyph files are modern vector redrawings. No image pixels or underlying archaeological inscription were visually inspected here; captions should be read as script-style candidates, not as verified facsimiles of particular artifacts.
The opened reconstruction and lexical reference pages do not resolve the graphic origin, and no sound component is proposed for 白.

items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 白 in oracle-script style. Early 白 forms are reported in oracle-bone divination texts, but the proposed object behind the shape is disputed.

items.caption: A modern rendering of 白 in the seal-script tradition associated with Shuowen. Xu Shen's explanation describes the graph through 入 and 二; it should be treated as a historical analysis, not proof of the earlier shape's origin.

limitations.text: These are modern vector redrawings labeled by script style, not photographs of ancient artifacts. Pixel-level visual inspection was not performed in this research stage.
The source pages identify source image records and reuse terms, but a glyph's script-style label alone does not establish a particular inscription's exact date or provenance.
